content: Table 3 shows the results of our two question answering models. It is clear that KVMemNet achieves better P@1 scores on both dev and test sets than PCNet. The reason is that candidate answers of PCNet come from the “anchor” point along 1-hop or 2-hop paths. However, the correct answer might not be connected due to the quality of anchor detection. On the dev set, we observe that only 69.6% of correct answers can be covered by the set of candidate answers in PCNet, which apparently limits the upper bound of the approach. This is addressed in KVMemNet because all the arguments are candidate answers. Both PCNet and KVMemNet outperform our implementation of BIBREF17 bordes2014question, since the latter ignores word order. We incorporate each of the four KBs separately into PCNet and KVMemNet, and find that incorporating external KBs could bring improvements.
